pass_a_gloss: Logos 4. [Lemma, Isaiah 49:1-3:] Hear me, islands, and pay attention, nations; through much time it will stand, says the Lord. From the belly of my mother he called my name, and set my mouth like a sharp sword, and under the shelter of his hand he hid me. He set me like a chosen arrow, and in his quiver he sheltered me, and said to me: You are my servant, Israel, and in you I will be glorified. Having benefited Israel through very many exhortations and counsels, he moves the teaching of the mystery onto the flocks of the nations, and indeed makes the mystery of Christ white [clear] to them again, through which they were going, having let go the cattle-like and accursed life, to be brought back into the way of life most dear to him, and to receive into mind the true light; so as to know clearly who is God by nature and truly, and the nature that rules over all. And he calls out to the islands, which indeed we say are the Churches of Christ, as lying in a sea, clearly the surge of the present life, and surrounded by unbearable onsets of waves, persecutions clearly and troubles, which the enemies of the truth, and those fighting against the calling of God, bring upon them. About such islands it has been said in very many places in the God-inspired Scripture. And the blessed David also sings somewhere and says: The Lord reigned, let the earth exult, let many islands be glad. For when Christ reigned over the [world] under heaven, having taken all under hand, and having torn it out of the tyranny of the demons, then also exulted, that is, became full of gladness, the Churches throughout all the earth. For that the prophet in these, having named islands, shows the Churches from nations would become clear through the things next. For he added at once to the 'Hear me, islands' the 'Pay attention, nations'. Then he says that, Through much time it will stand, says the Lord. He promises, as I said, the showing forth of the Saviour of us all, Jesus Christ, and that, being God, the Word converses with those on the earth in a form like ours. Except that the time then was of prophecy, and not yet of the very manifestation of the things, he shows, saying that through much time the thing promised will stand, clearly, or the thing being prophesied. What then is this? The very person of the Saviour was brought in, saying: From the belly of my mother he called my name. It happened [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: Logos 4. “Listen to me, you islands, and pay attention, you nations. After a long time it will stand, says the Lord. From my mother’s womb He called my name, and He made my mouth like a sharp sword, and He hid me under the shelter of His hand. He made me like a chosen arrow, and He sheltered me in His quiver, and He said to me, ‘You are My servant, Israel, and in you I will be glorified’” (Isaiah 49:1-3).

Having helped Israel by a great many exhortations and counsels, he moves his teaching of the mystery over to the flocks of the nations, and again makes the mystery of Christ clear to them. Through it they were to leave their brutish and accursed life, be brought back to the way of life dearest to Him, and receive the true light into their minds, so as to know clearly who is God by nature and in truth, the nature that rules over all things.

He addresses the islands, which we say are the Churches of Christ. They lie as if in a sea, that is, in the surge of the present life, and are surrounded by the unbearable onset of waves, that is, by persecutions and troubles, which the enemies of the truth, who fight against God’s calling, bring upon them. Of such islands the God-inspired Scripture speaks in very many places. Blessed David too sings somewhere and says: “The Lord has become King; let the earth rejoice; let the many islands be glad” (Psalm 97:1). For when Christ became King over the whole world under heaven, taking it all into His hand and wrenching it from the tyranny of the demons, then the Churches throughout the whole earth rejoiced, that is, were filled with gladness.

That the prophet, in calling them islands here, means the Churches drawn from the nations will become clear from what follows. For right after “Listen to me, you islands,” he added, “Pay attention, you nations.” Then he says: “After a long time it will stand, says the Lord.” As I said, he promises the manifestation of Jesus Christ, the Savior of us all, and that the Word, though He is God, lives among those on earth in a form like ours (compare Baruch 3:38). Yet he shows that the time then was a time of prophecy, not yet of the events themselves coming to light, by saying that after a long time it will stand, namely what was promised, that is, what was being prophesied.

choices.english: the islands, which we say are the Churches of Christ
choices.why: Cyril reads the islands as Churches set in the sea of this life.

choices.english: makes the mystery of Christ clear
choices.why: καταλευκαίνω, to make white or bright; the mystery is made plain to the nations.
The life of the nations before Christ, likened to that of cattle.

choices.english: After a long time it will stand
choices.why: Cyril takes it of the prophesied coming that had not yet arrived.
rejected: It will stand for a long time

choices.term: συν- αναστρέφεται τοῖς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς
choices.english: lives among those on earth in a form like ours
choices.why: Echoes Baruch 3:38, applied to the Incarnation.
